shortDescription: Chicago Board of Trade front-month corn futures fell on Thursday as plummeting wheat prices dragged the grains complex lower.

children: Chicago Board of Trade front-month corn futures fell on Thursday as plummeting wheat prices dragged the grains complex lower.

The Department of Agriculture on Thursday said new-crop U.S. corn export sales in the week ended August 27 were at 1,986,400 metric tons, above trade estimates for 500,000 to 1,600,000 tons. The agency also reported net cancellations of 829,600 tons of old-crop sales.
The corn market has been supported since last month by falling expectations for U.S. harvest yields.

A farmer survey conducted by agricultural commodity brokerage and analysis firm Allendale forecast the U.S. 2026 corn crop at 15.833 billion bushels, with an average yield of 178.7 bushels per acre, the company said on Wednesday.
Allendale's U.S. corn estimates were below the USDA's latest outlook for a corn crop of 16.013 billion bushels and an average yield of 180.7 bushels per acre.
The consultancy StoneX raised its estimate for Brazil's 2026/27 first corn crop to 29.3 million tons, from 28.7 million tons in its previous forecast.
The yield survey, conducted from August 17 to 28, was based on producer-calculated yields in 25 states covering 88% of U.S. corn production.
settled 2-3/4 cents lower at $5.40-3/4 per bushel.
